rows.annotation: DUF7844 family exported protein involved in tolerance to benzethonium chloride and benzalkonium chloride.
rows.evidence: Homologs at 73.9–75.6% identity show strong fitness defects under benzethonium chloride or benzalkonium chloride stress, supporting quaternary ammonium compound tolerance. The query contains DUF7844 and an Lnb N-terminal periplasmic domain; its cleavable signal peptide and absence of membrane-spanning segments support a soluble exported protein. A 97.1%-identity homolog is annotated as a conserved exported protein of unknown function.
rows.reasoning_trace: Tier A is supported by replicated, stressor-specific fitness phenotypes in close homologs; this establishes a physiological association without resolving molecular mechanism. Available evidence includes homolog summaries, fitness, domains, neighborhoods, STRING associations, and query topology, but no cofitness or direct biochemical characterization. The 42%-identity SmeY summary suggests efflux association, whereas direct topology supports a soluble exported protein; an integral RND transporter assignment is therefore unsupported. The broad metallopeptidase fold and STRING MtfA label do not establish protease activity or ptsG regulation.

Predicted class: SP
Signal peptide: residues 1-22 (cleavable)
Membrane-spanning segments: none (neither alpha-helical nor beta-strand)
Topology: signal peptide 1-22; extracellular/outside 23-651
Meaning: the protein has a cleavable signal peptide and NO membrane-spanning segment of either kind. The mature protein is therefore SOLUBLE AND EXPORTED -- periplasmic or secreted -- rather than membrane-embedded. It is not an integral membrane protein and not a beta-barrel.
[[END MEMBRANE TOPOLOGY PREDICTION]]
rows.conservation_breadth:
[[BEGIN CONSERVATION BREADTH]]
Counted over EVERY homolog found for this query, before the per-source display caps that apply to the other evidence blocks.
Distinct organisms with a homolog: 14 (in 4 genera)
Query organism: Pseudomonas putida
Organisms OTHER than the query's own with a homolog: 13 (3 genera other than Pseudomonas)
%Identity to query across these homologs: 36.7-97.1
Meaning: breadth of conservation, not function. A homolog in an organism other than the query's own is evidence the protein is real and under selection even when no function can be named, and supports calling it a CONSERVED hypothetical protein; homologs confined to the query's own organism do not. More organisms and more genera mean broader conservation. This NEVER constrains the specific function.
[[END CONSERVATION BREADTH]]
